utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: First of all, I want to mention a letter which I received from Mr. Milan Lukic. Mr. Lukic, the matter that you raised in the letter, I must inform you, is one that can only be addressed by the Trial Chamber. Of course, you may not know all the procedures of the Tribunal. You are represented by counsel, and matters relating to the trial must be presented in the usual way through counsel. Mr. Alarid, today, like many other days, no Defence witnesses available for testimony. I understand that arrangements are in place to bring four witnesses next week. We are scheduled to sit Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday of next week, and I hope that the production will be better. But quite frankly, the situation cannot be allowed to continue, Mr. Alarid. We have been reviewing the progress of the Defence case. It is lamentably slow. Eleven witnesses have been heard in 12 sitting days, spread over a period of more than two months since the close of the first Defence case. Even taking into account the winter recess and two extra days on which the Chamber did not sit, a total of 12 sitting days have been lost. This is more than 50 percent of the time available to you so far, and 30 percent or a third of the time available overall. The date of the 10th of March for completion of the presentation of the Defence case remains. Only 12 sitting days remain in February, plus 6 in March, and you still have a potential 30 witnesses to call. Of these, six are experts, and these may be cross-examined, likely to last at least two days. We calculate that you would need to call all of your other witnesses within the next two to three weeks. Otherwise, you may run out of time. I bring this matter to your attention. It has been brought to your attention before, and the Chamber will be considering what steps, what measures may be taken to address it. I turn to some matters arising from motions before the Chamber. There is a Defence motion pending for protective measures for two of the witnesses to be heard next week. Ms. Sartorio, the Chamber needs to have an expedited response to these requests. Are you in a position to respond orally now or do you need a short time in which to file a written submission, in which event that would have to be no later than 4.00 p.m. today, or perhaps Monday the 9th?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was our intent to address the motions for protective orders with regard to each witness when the witness came to testify. That's our plan. If you want something earlier, we're happy to submit something, but we thought it would be just more expeditious to address them when the witness came.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I am reminded that one disadvantage of that is that the witness does not know before travelling, whether that witness will receive protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: That's a fair statement, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In those circumstances, yes, I think you should file the written response. This, of course, doesn't mean that in exceptional circumstances we won't hear an oral request, you know. Turning to the Defence experts, we had ordered written submissions by the parties by last Monday, 2nd February, on a matter relating to Dr. Hall. We have received a submission from the Prosecution, but none from the Defence. Mr. Alarid, we have to resolve this matter quickly. Do you have a position on this or may we take it that you have received information you sought as to the relevant jurisprudence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The truth of the matter is, Your Honours, we were in Bosnia when the order came down, and so we didn't get that until just before we were supposed to visit the client in jail on Monday. That's why we didn't file a response. We filed a motion for extension of time with the Court, just simply asking for the 14 days normally allowed for, and it's already been filed, so that was the one of our submissions from last night that did that. We simply asked for the 14 days normally allowed for such a motion and response time. And I understand the Court can enlarge or reduce the time, based on exceptional circumstances and times of the case, but I would ask the Court to consider the fact that our limited resources -- I mean, we really only have so many man hours between Danny and I to put in a particular day as we try and cover all our duties in relation to the case, not just witness organisations but continued prosecution of legal issues, and preparation for witnesses, and just communications with clients, communications with the OTP, communications with WVS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, you have filed a motion. We'll consider it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: As for the remaining three experts, can you confirm that they are now available and will be provided to the Prosecution, the reports?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, yes, all notices, reports are being completed. We filed them all last night. They should be, and in response to Mr. Groome's, they just haven't hit the e-mail yet, but they were filed late last night, so all reports are in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Unless there are any other matters that the parties wish to raise, we will adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, actually, we do have one. Just to let you know what's coming down the pike, and I would like to ask the OTP and the Court for some assistance in this matter. We believe that we have located two victims of the Pionirska Street fire alive and well. One of the complicating factors is that we have not received the date of birth, father's name nor ID numbers that were registered to these people, because, as you know, Annex A is, I think, painfully short on information of identification and only puts us in the main direction. But we believe that we have found two of the named victims, one in the United States, one in Austria. In order to confirm and get proof of life, we would need as much information on the Annex A's named individuals as possible. And it's our understanding, just like in the United States, where we have a personal identification number, a social security number, Bosnia had in place the same ID requirements or similar ID requirements; and it would be extremely helpful if we had those identification numbers to assist, INS or both the immigration services of both Austria and the United States to comply with our request for assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Sartorio, are you in a position to provide that information?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, certainly not -- well, first of all, it would be a lot easier if they gave us the names of the two witnesses, if we submitted a request, but we're going to have to go through a formal request for assistance to the United States Immigration Service or Social Security Department. They don't give our social security numbers just by request from us. So that could take a long time. But if we ask for 70 witnesses, that's going to take longer than if they tell us the names of the two witnesses that they think are alive and well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, no, that's misstating our request -- or misunderstanding our request, rather. It's simply, no, we want the original Bosnian identification numbers that should have accompanied, we assume based on the research from the OTP investigation. The proof of death in this case is unorthodox. We had a single witness come in, look at this list and say all these people were there, and that was about the extent of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You're trying to get the original Bosnian identification number of what, of whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Of the list of victims, the entire list of victims, because we're looking for them all right now, Your Honour. I mean, I'm not asking for the OTP to do my work. I simply want them to give me the information I think they should have had as part of an ordinary investigation from the outset.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can certainly give them the information we have, but I certain we already gave them the information we had in the disclosure that we made to them of all the documents that we have involving this case. So I don't believe that we're obligated to go out and find this information. And it's, again, they need to go through the record. They want us to do the work by going through records of missing persons and death certificates, and they have all of the documents that are pertinent to this case and the victims in this case, and they simply should just have to do the work themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. She has spoken, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, my response is this is a homicide case. It's their job to prove death. It was done in a very unorthodox way as to how I'm normally used to it, but of course I'm normally used to one person being dead, not a slew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In their view, they have done their job. If their case is defective, well, you make that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I guess that is a good point, I guess. I'm not sure how to respond to that, other than that's a good point. But other than that, Your Honour, I mean, I think if there's a high likelihood that this trial is operating with some of the named victims alive, then that is a serious consideration; and I would ask you to consider the experts reports as filed, as bolstering our position that the possibility that these crimes did not occur or did not occur in the manner in which some witnesses believe they did, by virtue of perspective and ability to observe; that if we are saying that Milan Lukic killed 60 people, but a percentage of them show up alive, then how can we be assured, without some other form of proof of death which is more regular and accepted in the judicial systems around the world, then that is a serious problem for this case if we are bringing up alive people at this juncture in the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Alarid. We are adjourned. Anything else, Ms. Sartorio?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So we'll adjourned until Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 9th day of February, 2009, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 10.05 a.m.,
